hero: A pediatric peritoneal dialysis clinic in a Philippine hospital. A Filipino pediatric nephrologist kneels to examine the knees of a 12-year-old girl standing with mild knock-knees, wearing shorts and slippers; her mother stands beside her holding a folder of laboratory results and a small cooler bag. A dietitian at a side table arranges a few food packages and a plate of rice and egg. Warm daylight. No text.

figures.teaches: In pediatric CKD anemia, iron status and correctable causes come before an ESA.
figures.content: Top box 'Screen: CBC, reticulocytes, ferritin, TSAT; age-defined Hb cutoffs'. Branch 1 'Ferritin <45 ng/mL' to 'Start iron (oral or IV by preference)'. Branch 2 'Ferritin <100 and TSAT <40%, or ferritin 100-300 and TSAT <25%' to 'Iron indicated'. Monitoring box: 'Iron every 3 months; withhold if ferritin >700 or TSAT >=40%; stop during active infection'. Next box 'Look for other causes'. Final box 'Consider ESA: subcutaneous, lowest effective dose, Hb every 2-4 weeks'. Side warning: 'Avoid transfusion before transplant: HLA sensitization'.

figures.teaches: CKD-MBD reshapes the growing skeleton and, over years, the arteries.
figures.content: Left: kidney icon 'Phosphate excretion falls'. Arrows to 'FGF23 rises', 'Calcitriol falls', 'Calcium tends low', converging on enlarged parathyroid 'PTH rises'. Right: child's leg with knock-knee and enlarged growth plate labeled 'Disordered growth plate', hip inset 'Slipped epiphysis'. Bottom: artery cross-section with calcium deposits labeled 'Vascular calcification'. Badge: '14 of 16 aged 20-30 on dialysis had coronary calcium; none under 20'. Badge: 'KDIGO 2017: infant length at least quarterly (1B)'.

card: A Filipino girl standing in a clinic in shorts and slippers while a doctor gently examines her knees, her mother holding a folder of results.
